title: Submandibular gland excision
text: Submandibular gland excision, through the neck. In this film we follow the operation step by step on a three dimensional model, and look closely at the three nerves at risk: the marginal mandibular, the lingual and the hypoglossal.

title: Position and incision
text: The patient lies supine, with the neck extended and the head turned to the opposite side. A skin crease incision is marked at least three to four centimetres, about two finger breadths, below the lower border of the mandible, over the lower part of the gland. Placing it this low keeps it away from the marginal mandibular nerve.

title: Subplatysmal flap
text: Platysma is divided along the line of the incision, and the upper flap is raised in the plane just deep to it. The marginal mandibular nerve lies just deep to this plane, on the investing fascia, so the dissection does not go deeper than the fascia yet.

title: Protect the marginal mandibular nerve
text: The investing fascia is incised over the lower part of the gland. The facial vein is found on the surface of the gland, ligated low, and reflected upwards together with the fascia. This is the Hayes Martin manoeuvre. The nerve, which lies superficial to the vein, is carried up safely with the flap.

title: Distal facial artery
text: At the upper border of the gland, where the facial artery hooks over the mandible, the artery is ligated and divided, or dissected off the gland if it is to be preserved. The marginal mandibular nerve is kept in view throughout.

title: Mobilise the gland and expose mylohyoid
text: The lower part of the gland is freed from the digastric tendon, and the gland is freed forwards off mylohyoid, dividing the nerve to mylohyoid and its vessels. The free posterior border of mylohyoid is then retracted forwards, opening the deep part of the dissection.

title: Lingual nerve and ganglion
text: The gland is pulled downwards and backwards. The lingual nerve appears as a V shape, drawn down by the submandibular ganglion. The branches of the ganglion are clipped and divided close to the gland, and the lingual nerve itself is preserved.

title: Hypoglossal nerve
text: The hypoglossal nerve lies lower down, on hyoglossus, below the duct and deep to the digastric tendon, with its accompanying veins. The dissection is kept on the capsule of the gland, and venous bleeding is controlled under direct vision, never by blind clamping.

title: Duct and proximal facial artery
text: The duct is followed forwards and ligated as far anteriorly as possible, especially when it contains stones, and then divided. The proximal facial artery is ligated where it emerges from deep to the posterior belly of digastric, and the gland is removed. Bleeding is checked, a drain is placed if needed, and the wound is closed in layers.

title: Structures at risk
text: To summarise, the structures at risk are the marginal mandibular nerve, the lingual nerve, the hypoglossal nerve, and the facial artery. This film is for education only. Always check surgical detail against current atlases and senior guidance.
